items.prompt:
The Kanem-Bornu empire was located around which body of water?

A) Lake Chad
B) River Niger
C) Atlantic Ocean
D) Gulf of Guinea

The introduction of firearms and Turkish military advisers into Kanem-Bornu is associated with the reign of:

A) Oba Ewuare
B) Usman dan Fodio
C) Mai Idris Alooma
D) Jaja of Opobo

mcq_options.text: Salt and slaves across the Sahara

items.prompt:
A major source of wealth for the Kanem-Bornu empire was its control of the trade in:

A) Cocoa to Europe
B) Crude oil to America
C) Rubber to Asia
D) Salt and slaves across the Sahara
items.correct_answer: D) Salt and slaves across the Sahara

items.prompt:
The legendary founder of the Hausa states in Hausa tradition is:

A) Bayajidda
B) Oduduwa
C) Oranmiyan
D) Sundiata

The seven original Hausa states are commonly referred to as the:

A) Banza Bakwai
B) Hausa Bakwai
C) Sokoto Caliphate
D) Oyo Mesi

Kano and Katsina rose to prominence largely because they were important centres of:

A) Crude oil refining
B) Cocoa farming
C) Trans-Saharan trade
D) Coal mining

The walled cities of the Hausa states were built mainly to:

A) Store crude oil
B) House missionaries
C) Mine gold
D) Provide defence and control trade
items.correct_answer: D) Provide defence and control trade

items.prompt:
The Oyo empire was a powerful state of which ethnic group?

A) Yoruba
B) Igbo
C) Hausa
D) Tiv

The official who led the Oyo Mesi and could compel a failing Alaafin to commit suicide was the:

A) Are-Ona-Kakanfo
B) Oba
C) Bashorun
D) Emir

The military strength of the Oyo empire depended heavily on its use of:

A) Naval fleets
B) Gunpowder artillery
C) War elephants
D) Cavalry

The famous bronze and brass works were produced in the kingdom of:

A) Nupe
B) Benin
C) Jukun
D) Igala

The ruler of the Benin kingdom carried the title of:

A) Emir
B) Obi
C) Oba
D) Alaafin

The Benin punitive expedition of 1897 was carried out by the:

A) British
B) French
C) Portuguese
D) Germans

Traditional Igbo society is best described as politically:

A) Highly centralised
B) Decentralised
C) A single empire
D) A caliphate

The Nri kingdom among the Igbo was significant mainly for its:

A) Large standing army
B) Trans-Saharan cavalry
C) Religious and ritual authority
D) Naval fleet

Decisions in many traditional Igbo communities were taken through:

A) A single hereditary king
B) An appointed emir
C) A colonial governor
D) Village assemblies and age grades
items.correct_answer: D) Village assemblies and age grades

items.prompt:
The Kwararafa confederacy was associated with which people?

A) Jukun
B) Yoruba
C) Edo
D) Efik

The Igala kingdom was ruled by a king who bore the title:

A) Oba
B) Attah
C) Emir
D) Obong

The trading city-states of the Niger Delta such as Bonny and Calabar grew rich from:

A) Gold mining
B) Cocoa exports
C) The slave and palm-oil trade
D) Coal mining
items.correct_answer: C) The slave and palm-oil trade

items.prompt:
The political unit that organised trade in the Niger Delta city-states was the:

A) Oyo Mesi
B) Sokoto Caliphate
C) Ogboni society
D) House system

The dominant religion among the rulers of Kanem-Bornu was:

A) Islam
B) Christianity
C) Buddhism
D) Hinduism

mcq_options.text: North Africa and the Middle East

items.prompt:
Kanem-Bornu maintained diplomatic and trade links across the Sahara especially with:

A) South America
B) North Africa and the Middle East
C) Western Europe by sea
D) East Asia
items.correct_answer: B) North Africa and the Middle East

items.prompt:
Which of the following was a famous walled trading city of the Hausa states?

A) Benin
B) Ile-Ife
C) Kano
D) Opobo

The Hausa states never formed a single empire mainly because they were:

A) Ruled by one emperor
B) Part of Oyo
C) A Portuguese colony
D) Separate, rival city-states

The capital of the old Oyo empire was:

A) Oyo-Ile
B) Lagos
C) Kano
D) Calabar

The supreme military commander of the Oyo empire was the:

A) Bashorun
B) Are-Ona-Kakanfo
C) Oba
D) Bali

The ruler of Benin during the 1897 British expedition was:

A) Oba Ewuare
B) Jaja of Opobo
C) Nana Olomu
D) Oba Ovonramwen

In Yoruba tradition, the cradle and spiritual home of the Yoruba people is:

A) Ile-Ife
B) Oyo
C) Benin
D) Kano

Ile-Ife is famous in art history for its naturalistic terracotta and:

A) Oil paintings
B) Bronze heads
C) Iron ships
D) Glass windows

mcq_options.text: Title societies and the council of elders

items.prompt:
A common feature of Igbo political organisation was the importance of:

A) A single hereditary emperor
B) A standing cavalry
C) A colonial governor
D) Title societies and the council of elders
items.correct_answer: D) Title societies and the council of elders

items.prompt:
Which of these was a trading city-state of the Niger Delta?

A) Bonny
B) Sokoto
C) Kano
D) Ibadan

Centralised kingdoms such as Oyo, Benin and Kanem-Bornu differed from the Igbo mainly in having:

A) No trade at all
B) Strong central rulers
C) No religion
D) European parliaments

A common economic basis for the rise of early Nigerian states was control of:

A) Crude-oil exports
B) Railways
C) Trade and tribute
D) Stock markets

The trans-Saharan trade linked West Africa with which region?

A) South America
B) East Asia
C) Australia
D) North Africa and the Mediterranean
items.correct_answer: D) North Africa and the Mediterranean

items.prompt:
The animal that made long-distance trade across the Sahara possible was the:

A) Camel
B) Horse
C) Donkey
D) Ox

Which commodity from the Sahara was exchanged for West African gold?

A) Cocoa
B) Salt
C) Rubber
D) Tea

The most important West African export across the Sahara in the medieval period was:

A) Crude oil
B) Cotton textiles
C) Gold
D) Coal

Besides gold, an important human 'commodity' traded across the Sahara was:

A) Tourists
B) Pilgrims
C) Soldiers
D) Slaves

A major cultural effect of the trans-Saharan trade on West Africa was the spread of:

A) Islam
B) Christianity
C) Buddhism
D) Hinduism

mcq_options.text: Generated wealth and tax revenue for rulers

items.prompt:
The trans-Saharan trade contributed to the rise of large states because it:

A) Reduced population
B) Generated wealth and tax revenue for rulers
C) Ended farming
D) Stopped warfare
items.correct_answer: B) Generated wealth and tax revenue for rulers

items.prompt:
Which city became a famous centre of trade and Islamic learning on the southern edge of the Sahara?

A) Lagos
B) Accra
C) Timbuktu
D) Cape Town

Kano and Katsina served the trans-Saharan trade mainly as:

A) Naval ports
B) Mining towns
C) Mission stations
D) Commercial and manufacturing hubs

The first Europeans to begin sea trade along the West African coast were the:

A) Portuguese
B) British
C) Germans
D) Americans

The trans-Atlantic slave trade developed mainly to supply labour for:

A) Saharan salt mines
B) Plantations in the Americas
C) European factories
D) Indian tea estates

The trans-Atlantic trade is often described as 'triangular' because it linked:

A) Africa, Asia and Europe
B) America, Asia and Australia
C) Europe, Africa and the Americas
D) Europe, Asia and Africa
items.correct_answer: C) Europe, Africa and the Americas

items.prompt:
In the triangular trade, manufactured goods were typically shipped from Europe to:

A) the Americas
B) Asia
C) Australia
D) Africa

European traders commonly exchanged firearms, cloth and spirits in Africa for:

A) Enslaved people
B) Cocoa
C) Rubber
D) Gold coins

A major demographic effect of the trans-Atlantic slave trade on West Africa was:

A) Rapid population growth
B) Loss of population
C) Total depopulation of cities
D) Mass immigration

mcq_options.text: Captives could be sold to European traders

items.prompt:
The trans-Atlantic slave trade encouraged inter-state wars in West Africa mainly because:

A) Europeans banned all trade
B) Farming became impossible
C) Captives could be sold to European traders
D) Gold was exhausted
items.correct_answer: C) Captives could be sold to European traders

mcq_options.text: Distortion of local economies toward slave raiding

items.prompt:
An economic consequence of the slave trade for West African societies was:

A) Industrial revolution
B) Free education
C) Currency unification
D) Distortion of local economies toward slave raiding
items.correct_answer: D) Distortion of local economies toward slave raiding

items.prompt:
Britain abolished the trans-Atlantic slave trade in the year:

A) 1807
B) 1914
C) 1960
D) 1885

After abolition, the British navy patrol that intercepted slave ships was based partly at:

A) Lagos only
B) Freetown, Sierra Leone
C) Cape Town
D) Liverpool

The trade that Europeans encouraged in West Africa to replace the slave trade was the trade in:

A) Crude oil
B) Diamonds
C) Palm oil and other 'legitimate' goods
D) Coal
items.correct_answer: C) Palm oil and other 'legitimate' goods

items.prompt:
A leading British abolitionist who campaigned against the slave trade was:

A) Cecil Rhodes
B) Lord Lugard
C) Mungo Park
D) William Wilberforce

The growth of 'legitimate trade' in the 19th century increased European interest in:

A) Controlling African coastal territory
B) Leaving Africa entirely
C) Abolishing all trade
D) Building Saharan railways

Caravans crossing the Sahara usually travelled in large groups mainly for:

A) Tax exemption
B) Religious pilgrimage only
C) Safety and shared resources
D) Sporting competition

Apart from gold and salt, items traded across the Sahara included kola nuts, leather and:

A) Crude oil
B) Television sets
C) Steel
D) Ivory

The trans-Saharan trade helped introduce into West Africa the use of:

A) Writing and Islamic scholarship
B) The steam engine
C) Electric light
D) The printing press

Djenne and Gao, like Timbuktu, were important towns of the:

A) Atlantic slave coast
B) Western Sudan trade
C) Congo basin
D) Nile valley

European forts and trading posts along the West African coast were known as:

A) Cathedrals
B) Universities
C) Castles or factories
D) Refineries

In the triangular trade, the brutal voyage carrying enslaved Africans across the Atlantic was called the:

A) Grand Tour
B) Long March
C) Silk Road
D) Middle Passage

Plantations in the Americas that relied on enslaved African labour produced mainly:

A) Sugar, cotton and tobacco
B) Crude oil
C) Cars
D) Computers

The trans-Atlantic slave trade enriched coastal middlemen in Africa while:

A) Industrialising the Sahara
B) Depopulating and destabilising the interior
C) Ending all warfare
D) Uniting all states
items.correct_answer: B) Depopulating and destabilising the interior

items.prompt:
The British naval squadron set up to suppress the slave trade after 1807 operated along the:

A) Mediterranean only
B) Indian Ocean only
C) West African coast
D) Pacific coast

The main 'legitimate' export of the Niger Delta in the 19th century was:

A) Cocoa
B) Crude oil
C) Cotton
D) Palm oil

Slavery itself (not just the trade) was abolished throughout the British Empire in:

A) 1833
B) 1807
C) 1914
D) 1960

The trans-Atlantic slave trade lasted for roughly:

A) Less than ten years
B) Over three centuries
C) Exactly fifty years
D) One year

mcq_options.text: Massive forced movement of people overseas

items.prompt:
Compared with the trans-Saharan trade, the trans-Atlantic trade was distinctive for its:

A) Use of camels
B) Reliance on salt
C) Massive forced movement of people overseas
D) Spread of Islam
items.correct_answer: C) Massive forced movement of people overseas

items.prompt:
Both the trans-Saharan and trans-Atlantic trades involved the export of:

A) Cars
B) Electricity
C) Newspapers
D) Enslaved people

The European conference that set rules for the partition of Africa met in:

A) Berlin
B) London
C) Paris
D) Lagos

The Berlin Conference that regulated the 'scramble for Africa' was held in:

A) 1914-1918
B) 1884-1885
C) 1939-1945
D) 1960

A principle agreed at the Berlin Conference was that a power claiming territory had to show:

A) Religious conversion
B) Free elections
C) Effective occupation
D) A written constitution

Lagos was annexed by Britain as a colony in the year:

A) 1914
B) 1960
C) 1900
D) 1861

The Royal Niger Company helped Britain control trade and territory in the:

A) Niger basin
B) Sahara desert
C) Congo basin
D) Nile valley

The Northern and Southern protectorates of Nigeria were amalgamated in:

A) 1900
B) 1914
C) 1960
D) 1885

The British governor who carried out the amalgamation of Nigeria in 1914 was:

A) Lord Macpherson
B) Sir Hugh Clifford
C) Lord Lugard
D) Sir John Macpherson

mcq_options.text: Joined diverse peoples without their consent

items.prompt:
A long-term criticism of the 1914 amalgamation is that it:

A) Granted immediate independence
B) Abolished all chiefs
C) Created a republic
D) Joined diverse peoples without their consent
items.correct_answer: D) Joined diverse peoples without their consent

items.prompt:
The system of governing colonies through existing traditional rulers was called:

A) Indirect rule
B) Direct rule
C) Assimilation
D) Association

Indirect rule is most associated with which colonial administrator in Nigeria?

A) Nnamdi Azikiwe
B) Lord Lugard
C) Herbert Macaulay
D) Obafemi Awolowo

Indirect rule worked most smoothly in which part of Nigeria?

A) The Eastern Igbo areas
B) The Niger Delta creeks
C) The North
D) Lagos colony

Indirect rule was least successful among the Igbo mainly because they:

A) Had a powerful emir
B) Spoke French
C) Were already independent
D) Lacked centralised chiefs

To impose indirect rule in the East, the British appointed officials known as:

A) Warrant chiefs
B) Obas
C) Emirs
D) District officers

The unpopularity of warrant chiefs contributed directly to the:

A) Berlin Conference
B) Aba Women's Riot of 1929
C) Atlantic Charter
D) 1914 amalgamation

The French colonial policy that aimed to turn Africans into 'black Frenchmen' was:

A) Indirect rule
B) Apartheid
C) Assimilation
D) Federation

mcq_options.text: Reduce the power of traditional rulers

items.prompt:
Compared with British indirect rule, French direct rule tended to:

A) Strengthen local kings
B) Grant immediate independence
C) Avoid taxation
D) Reduce the power of traditional rulers
items.correct_answer: D) Reduce the power of traditional rulers

items.prompt:
Colonial economic policy in Nigeria emphasised the production of:

A) Cash crops for export
B) Heavy industry
C) Computer technology
D) Crude-oil refining

mcq_options.text: Move raw materials to the coast for export

items.prompt:
The colonial railway in Nigeria was built mainly to:

A) Provide free passenger travel
B) Move raw materials to the coast for export
C) Connect mosques
D) Carry tourists
items.correct_answer: B) Move raw materials to the coast for export

items.prompt:
Under colonial rule, the highest official representing the British Crown in Nigeria was the:

A) Prime Minister
B) President
C) Governor
D) Sultan

Native courts and native treasuries were features of which system?

A) Direct rule
B) Federalism
C) Republicanism
D) Indirect rule

mcq_options.text: Western education and a common language of administration

items.prompt:
One positive legacy often credited to colonial rule in Nigeria was the introduction of:

A) Western education and a common language of administration
B) Crude-oil wealth
C) Multi-party democracy
D) Total self-government
items.correct_answer: A) Western education and a common language of administration

mcq_options.text: Dependence on export of raw materials

items.prompt:
A negative effect of colonial rule on Nigerian economies was:

A) Rapid industrialisation
B) Dependence on export of raw materials
C) Self-sufficiency in goods
D) Abolition of taxation
items.correct_answer: B) Dependence on export of raw materials

items.prompt:
The period of rapid European seizure of African territory in the late 19th century is called the:

A) Middle Passage
B) Cold War
C) Scramble for Africa
D) Industrial Revolution

The British consolidated control of Northern Nigeria in the early 1900s largely through the conquest of the:

A) Oyo empire
B) Benin kingdom
C) Asante kingdom
D) Sokoto Caliphate

The charter of the Royal Niger Company was revoked and its territory taken over by the British government in:

A) 1900
B) 1861
C) 1914
D) 1960

mcq_options.text: Cheaper and needed fewer European staff

items.prompt:
A practical reason the British favoured indirect rule was that it was:

A) More democratic
B) Cheaper and needed fewer European staff
C) Designed to grant independence
D) Required by the United Nations
items.correct_answer: B) Cheaper and needed fewer European staff

mcq_options.text: Men with no traditional right to rule

items.prompt:
Warrant chiefs were resented partly because they were often:

A) Elected by the people
B) European officials
C) Men with no traditional right to rule
D) Religious leaders
items.correct_answer: C) Men with no traditional right to rule

items.prompt:

A) Warrant chiefs
B) Emirs
C) Settlers
D) The assimilated (evolues)

B) Cocoa
C) Crude oil
D) Rubber

A major cash crop of Western Nigeria under colonial rule was:

A) Groundnuts
B) Cocoa
C) Coal
D) Cotton only

Colonial revenue in Nigeria was raised largely through:

A) Crude-oil sales
B) Tourism
C) Taxes and customs duties
D) Foreign aid only

A) Universal suffrage
B) Full independence

D) Elective representation

The 1929 Aba Women's Riot is best understood as a form of:

A) Religious festival
B) Anti-colonial protest

D) Election campaign

B) The United Nations

mcq_options.text: A ban by the United Nations
British protection of Islamic institutions under indirect rule

items.prompt:
Western education spread more slowly in the North than the South partly because of:

A) Lack of any people there
B) A ban by the United Nations
C) The civil war
D) British protection of Islamic institutions under indirect rule
items.correct_answer: D) British protection of Islamic institutions under indirect rule

items.prompt:

B) More European settlers

D) Religious conversion

mcq_options.text: Demonstrating organised mass protest against the colonial government

items.prompt:

A) Ending the slave trade

items.correct_answer: C) Demonstrating organised mass protest against the colonial government

mcq_options.text: Returning with new ideas of freedom and equality

items.prompt:
Nigerian soldiers who fought in the Second World War contributed to nationalism by:

A) Supporting permanent colonial rule
B) Joining the Royal Niger Company
C) Founding mission schools
D) Returning with new ideas of freedom and equality
items.correct_answer: D) Returning with new ideas of freedom and equality

items.prompt:

A) Self-determination of peoples
B) Permanent colonial rule
C) Free trade in slaves
D) Partition of Africa

A) Apartheid
B) Pan-Africanism
C) Assimilation
D) Indirect rule

A) Lord Lugard
B) Cecil Rhodes

D) Mungo Park

B) Flora Shaw

C) Free trade

mcq_options.text: Constitutional agitation, parties and the press

items.prompt:
Nigerian nationalists pursued their aims mainly through:

A) Armed guerrilla warfare
B) Foreign invasion
C) Religious crusades
D) Constitutional agitation, parties and the press
items.correct_answer: D) Constitutional agitation, parties and the press

items.prompt:

A) Constitutional and non-violent

C) Decided by civil war
D) Imposed by the United Nations

African nationalism was strengthened by a shared grievance against:

A) Free trade

mcq_options.text: Revive African names, dress and religion

items.prompt:

B) End all trade
C) Restore the slave trade

items.correct_answer: D) Revive African names, dress and religion

items.prompt:

A) Action Group
B) NPC

A) Unfair taxation of women

C) Free trade
D) Railway building

mcq_options.text: Spread ideas and mobilise public opinion

items.prompt:

items.correct_answer: A) Spread ideas and mobilise public opinion

mcq_options.text: A colony could win independence from Britain

items.prompt:

items.prompt:

items.prompt:
